case_metadata.source: Ali Hadi DFIR Challenge #1 — Web Server Case
case_metadata.subject: Windows web server (XAMPP: Apache + MySQL + FileZilla) breached through the public web application
case_metadata.operating_system: Windows (XAMPP LAMP stack — Apache httpd, MySQL/mysqld, FileZilla FTP)
case_metadata.ground_truth_provenance: Ali Hadi official challenge questions (ashemery.com / Security4Arabs), cross-checked against public write-ups that confirm a Windows/XAMPP web-server compromise: web-application exploitation (SQL injection, command injection), web-shell deployment, and unauthorized account creation. The evidence_root is a Windows disk with xampp/, inetpub/, and Windows/ — not Linux.

ground_truth_findings.claim: Initial access via web-application exploitation — SQL injection against the XAMPP-hosted site
ground_truth_findings.rationale: Apache access.log records SQL-injection payloads from the attacker IP against the web application.

ground_truth_findings.claim: Command injection / remote code execution through the web application
ground_truth_findings.rationale: access.log shows command-injection request patterns that drive OS command execution on the host.

ground_truth_findings.claim: Web shell uploaded and accessed through the web application
ground_truth_findings.rationale: access.log contains web-shell upload requests followed by repeated shell access — a planted web shell.

ground_truth_findings.claim: Attacker source IP 192.168.56.102 generated high-volume malicious requests
ground_truth_findings.rationale: A single source IP dominates request volume with attack payloads, identifying the attacker.

ground_truth_findings.claim: Reconnaissance and vulnerability scanning of the web application
ground_truth_findings.rationale: access.log shows scanner user-agents and probing requests preceding the exploitation phase.
